Gens.fact: In ancient Rome, a gens ( or , Latin: [gẽːs]; pl.: gentes [ˈgɛnteːs]) was a family consisting of individuals who shared the same nomen gentilicium and who claimed descent from a common ancestor. A branch of a gens, sometimes identified by a distinct cognomen, was called a stirps (pl.: stirpes).

Gens.subject: Women & Society
Gens.question: It can also be translated as "clan", "kin", or "tribe", although the word tribus has a separate and distinct meaning in _____ culture
Gens.fact: The importance of the gens as a social structure declined considerably in imperial times, although the gentilicium continued to define the origins and dynasties of the ancient Romans, including the emperors. It can also be translated as "clan", "kin", or "tribe", although the word tribus has a separate and distinct meaning in Roman culture.

All of these peoples were eventually absorbed into the sphere of Roman culture.
